claims.claim: A coupled40way cross-entropy loss has no existing contraction framework.
claims.finding: For fixed labels, logsumexp(z)-z_y is globally sqrt2-Lipschitz in Euclidean logits because its gradient is softmax(z)-e_y. Cor4 supplies an unnormalized complexity bound with constant2. Samplewise contraction needs no iid assumption on the fixed design; population generalization requires the matching sampling and loss conditions.

claims.claim: Auxiliary epsilon_ik means there are n*40 independent training examples.
claims.finding: Independent signs appear only in the Rademacher complexity upper bound. The actual dataset remains n iid labeled examples in the paper multiclass example; no40task sample bonus.

claims.claim: Bounding Born scores in[0,1] makes the full native logit class bounded.
claims.finding: In the inspected mathematical head parameterization, setting decoder0 leaves arbitrary trainable bias. A centered bias direction remains unbounded after removing the common-softmax-shift direction. Finite trained weights or weight decay do not supply a predeclared hard function-class radius. No whole-training-pipeline no-regularization claim made.

claims.claim: The vector contraction inequality proves a sharing advantage.
claims.finding: The coupled class is contained in the coordinatewise product superset, but inclusion alone proves no strict or useful quantitative gap. Native shared preparation and value paths require full class/norm analysis; known Frobenius/trace-norm templates do not establish a new theorem or actual held-out Macro gain.

claims.claim: This failed direct bound invalidates oldL4 or all possible generalization analysis.
claims.finding: Only direct unbounded full-class and standard-contraction-as-novelty routes close. Localized/data-dependent/margin analyses with justified assumptions remain possible. No old empirical claim upgraded or revoked.
